data.hypothesis: The best persistent-team result (56b28747a297486d, 0.2292 s) is faster in aggregate than the per-timestep-region result (b67f9cc2abc34db6, 0.2376 s), while the serial baseline measured 0.4575 s. This candidate keeps a serial path for one-thread and small-work calls, and uses static row-level work sharing with a separate region per timestep only for larger thread budgets. Comparing its four-thread result with the persistent-team candidate tests whether repeated region creation offsets the parallel work; the serial one-thread path tests whether OpenMP setup is worth avoiding there. No speedup is assumed before measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these aggregate results to motivate a controlled comparison, not to infer which region lifetime wins at a particular thread count.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured serial baseline was 0.4575 s; the best persistent-team candidate was 0.2292 s, while a per-timestep-region candidate measured 0.2376 s. These aggregate means do not by themselves establish per-thread-count causality.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare serial at one thread and per-timestep regions at four threads against the corresponding baseline and persistent-team results under the official settings.

data.notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed. The serial path handles nonpositive or one-thread budgets and active widths below 16; larger calls use up to the supplied thread budget, capped by the number of z/y rows. The controller should verify complete outputs and boundaries, then measure at the official one- and four-core settings; this proposal has not been run or measured.
transformations: Factored the stencil row arithmetic into a shared inline row kernel used by serial and parallel steps.
Kept the existing six-step ping-pong computation and output initialization, using the serial implementation for one-thread budgets and small active widths.
Added static collapsed z/y row work-sharing in a separate OpenMP region per timestep for larger thread budgets, with num_threads derived from the supplied budget and capped by the number of rows.
